oewn-01463601-s.learner: so hateful that there can be no doubt about it.
examples: Oh, that abominable Mr. Darcy!
Can such abominable pride as his have ever done him good?

connotation.why: condemns its target outright, against a plain 'bad' or 'unpleasant'

oewn-01466592-v.learner: to put things in the right order, or in an order that follows a plan.
examples: everything was fitted up and arranged with a neatness and consistency, of which Elizabeth gave Charlotte all the credit.

oewn-01023638-v.learner: to make the plans and preparations needed for something.
examples: We arranged a meeting with the lawyer for Friday.

oewn-00737576-v.learner: to put thoughts, ideas, or events in time into an order.
examples: She arranged her ideas before she began to write.
I need to arrange my schedule for next week.

oewn-00038562-v.learner: to put something in place so that it looks nice.
examples: She arranged her hair before the dance.
He arranged the flowers in a tall vase.

oewn-01651668-v.learner: to plan an event, get it ready, and then make it happen.
examples: The club arranged a dance in the village hall and ran it themselves.

oewn-01709988-v.learner: to change a piece, such as a song, so that it can be performed in a different way.
examples: He arranged the old folk song for piano and voice.

oewn-01748949-v.learner: to set printed text out in a particular layout.
examples: The printer arranged the text in two columns on each page.

Her boy is forty now and has children of his own.

oewn-09890332-n.learner: a friendly, informal word for a grown man.
examples: He went out for a drink with the boys from work.

connotation.why: calls a grown man 'boy' where 'man' is the plain word

oewn-84496658-n.learner: an offensive, insulting word used for a Black man.
examples: Calling a Black man 'boy' was a way of insulting him.

connotation.why: ethnic slur aimed at Black men

oewn-13943868-n.learner: the state that something or someone is in at a certain time.
examples: But the spiritless condition which this event threw her into was shortly relieved

oewn-06783666-n.learner: a statement of what must be done or accepted as part of an agreement, usually used in the plural.
examples: These are conditions which, considering everything, I had no hesitation in complying with

oewn-06768279-n.learner: something that must be true first for something else to be valid or to have its effect.
examples: Trust is a necessary condition for any friendship to last.

oewn-13943462-n.learner: the way a person or thing exists, or the kind of life or being they have.
examples: to congratulate myself on the hope of relations whose condition in life is so decidedly beneath my own?
Fear of death is part of the human condition.

oewn-05831106-n.learner: a fact that you should keep in mind when you decide something.
examples: Before choosing, think about every condition: the cost, the time, and the risk.

oewn-13946473-n.learner: an illness, a disease, or some other health problem.
examples: She has a heart condition and must not run.

oewn-14569829-n.learner: how healthy and fit someone is, as in 'in condition' or 'out of condition'.
examples: After the long winter I was out of condition and could not run far.

oewn-05806871-n.learner: in an experiment, the way of doing things that is changed so that its effect can be compared with an unchanged control.
examples: Half the mice were placed in the test condition and half in the control condition.

oewn-00206498-n.learner: giving up what is good for yourself so that other people can have what is good for them.
examples: Her life was one of quiet denial, always putting her family's needs before her own.

oewn-07219061-n.learner: the act of refusing to do what is asked, for example by a request.
examples: if, under such a circumstance, I were to give a flat denial, and ride off as fast as I could.

oewn-07218900-n.learner: the act of saying that something people claim is not true.
examples: The minister's denial of the story came too late.

oewn-13483154-n.learner: in psychiatry, a way the mind protects itself by refusing to accept painful thoughts.
examples: After the diagnosis she was in denial for weeks.

connotation.why: said of a person, against a plain 'does not accept it'

oewn-01201240-n.learner: the answer someone accused gives in court, saying that the charges against them are not true.
examples: The court heard the defendant's denial of all the charges.

oewn-07495208-n.learner: a strong feeling of any kind.
examples: acknowledged, with the liveliest emotion, that she was the happiest creature in the world.
Mr. Darcy changed colour; but the emotion was short

oewn-06276128-n.learner: mail that is carried by a fast and well-run system.

oewn-03311330-n.learner: a fast train or bus that stops at only a few planned places.

oewn-01108365-n.learner: the fast carrying of goods from one place to another.
examples: The company ships its furniture by express.

oewn-06769118-n.learner: a statement that is not true.

oewn-00752233-n.learner: the act of making something false, for example by dishonestly changing papers or measures, or by making fakes.
examples: He was charged with falsehood for changing the figures in the company's books.

oewn-02355171-v.learner: to free a person or place from something.

oewn-04610439-n.learner: a small place where things are made by hand or by machine.
examples: In his shop behind the house, the carpenter builds chairs by hand.
